proofs.proof_tex:
Under \(\texttt{ass:one-unsupported-row}\) and
\(\texttt{ass:binary-free-row}\), the generalized unsupported-row objects
specialize to
\[
 \mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}=\{rstar\},
 \qquad
 \mathcal P_{\mathrm{free}}
 =\{(1-q,q):0\leq q\leq 1\}.
\]
Comparing \(\texttt{def:model-class}\) with
\(\texttt{def:finite-unsupported-model-class}\), all their other
membership requirements agree in this specialization: both use the same
finite schema and graph, induce the same source and target groundings,
require mutually independent distinct exogenous variables, exclude
exogenous relational parents, exclude any non-relational exogenous parent
shared by distinct ground endogenous variables, require type-shared finite
mechanisms, reproduce \(Psrc\), and use \(K\) at every
positive-source-support key.  The comparator-only uniform bound in
\(\texttt{ass:bounded-relational-parent-multisets}\) is not a membership
condition of either structural class and is not used in this comparison.
Consequently
\[
 \mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}=Mone.
\]
The definitions of the two queries then give
\(Q_{\mathrm{fin}}=Q\).  Replaying
\(\texttt{def:multivariate-target-polynomial}\) at
\(p_{rstar}=(1-q,q)\) performs exactly the substitutions defining \(F\).
Equivalently, this is the reduction proved in
\(\texttt{lem:polynomial-reduction}\).  Hence, for every \(q\in[0,1]\),
\[
 \Phi\bigl((1-q,q)\bigr)=F(q).
\]
Applying \(\texttt{thm:sharp-finite-unsupported-rows}\) to this
specialization proves
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1])
 =\left[\min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q),\max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)\right].
\]
In particular, the reverse inclusion is witnessed by compatible
finite-noise, type-shared models; the displayed set is not merely an outer
bound.

It remains to identify these two extrema with the declared algebraic
candidates.  If \(F\) is nonconstant and \(c\in(0,1)\) is a minimizer,
then for all sufficiently small \(h>0\),
\[
 \frac{F(c+h)-F(c)}{h}\geq0,
 \qquad
 \frac{F(c)-F(c-h)}{h}\leq0.
\]
Both quotients converge to \(F'(c)\), so \(F'(c)=0\).  Reversing the two
inequalities gives the same conclusion for an interior maximizer.  Thus
every optimizer is \(0\), \(1\), or a feasible distinct real root of
\(F'\), and therefore lies in \(Ccrit\) by
\(\texttt{def:critical-candidates}\).  Since \(Ccrit\subseteq[0,1]\) and
the global optimizers belong to \(Ccrit\),
\[
 \min_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=\min_{c\in Ccrit}F(c)=L,
 \qquad
 \max_{q\in[0,1]}F(q)=\max_{c\in Ccrit}F(c)=U.
\]
If \(F\) is constant, \(Ccrit\) contains the boundary candidates and all
its values equal that same constant, so the two equalities still hold.
This proves the unconditional structural assertion
\[
 \Theta=F([0,1])=[L,U].
\]

We now prove only the conditional comparator consequences stated in the
theorem.  By
\(\texttt{lem:ejaz-bareinboim-rho-markovian-scope}\), Definition 3.2 and
the Section 5 domain impose different requirements: the former gives the
\(\rho\)-Markovian exogenous-parent restrictions, whereas assumptions
(I)--(III) specify the domain on which Algorithm 1 and Corollary D.7 have
their soundness and completeness guarantee.  In particular, the global
relational-parent bound is not inferred from the finiteness of the listed
source and target groundings.

Fix an instance satisfying the two explicit comparator hypotheses in the
statement, and write \(\mathcal E\) for its compatible
Ejaz--Bareinboim class in the intersection with the Section 5 domain.
The second hypothesis is precisely the same-data, same-query inclusion
\[
 Mone\subseteq\mathcal E.
\]
If \(F\) is nonconstant, choose \(q_1,q_2\in[0,1]\) with
\(F(q_1)\neq F(q_2)\).  The already proved equality
\(\Theta=F([0,1])\) supplies \(M_1,M_2\in Mone\), both reproducing the
fixed source laws, such that
\[
 Q(M_1)=F(q_1)\neq F(q_2)=Q(M_2).
\]
The inclusion places both witnesses in \(\mathcal E\), so the causal query
is not point identified in \(\mathcal E\).  This is the claimed upward
transfer of nonidentification.  If Algorithm 1 reports
\(\mathsf{FAIL}\) on such an instance, that report does not change the
structural equality already proved for \(Mone\).  Conversely, inclusion
alone gives no upper or lower restriction on values attained by elements
of \(\mathcal E\setminus Mone\); it therefore gives neither sharpness of
\([L,U]\) nor equality of the two identified sets.

If \(F\) is constant, the structural part gives \(L=U\) on \(Mone\).
When the compatible classes coincide, substitution of that equality of
classes transfers the singleton conclusion.  When the inclusion is
strict, constancy on \(Mone\) says nothing about the query values of the
additional models in \(\mathcal E\setminus Mone\), so no such transfer is
valid.

Finally, unsupportedness alone does not force
\(\mathsf{FAIL}\).  Consider a finite, acyclic, two-node instance in the
Section 5 domain for which the supplied graph excludes every additional
shared-exogenous structure, so that the comparator and fully Markovian
compatible classes coincide.  Let \(A\) be a supported fair binary node,
let \(X\) use the single unsupported binary row with success probability
\(q\), take the intervention assignment to be empty, and set
\(B=\{A=X\}\).  Independence gives
\[
 P(B\mid\operatorname{do}(a))
 =P(A=0)P(X=0)+P(A=1)P(X=1)
 =(1-q)\frac{1}{2}+q\frac{1}{2}=\frac{1}{2}.
\]
Thus the row is target relevant but cancels from the query, and the
sound-and-complete identified-case procedure on this comparator-domain
instance cannot return \(\mathsf{FAIL}\).

As a load-bearing check on the shared-coordinate reduction, take two
independent target nodes using the same unsupported binary key and let
the event be exactly one success.  Type sharing gives the map
\[
 2q(1-q)\leq\frac{1}{2}.
\]
If type sharing is removed while the remaining finite acyclic structure
is retained, occurrence-specific choices \(q_1=1\) and \(q_2=0\) make
the event probability \(1\).  Hence the common coordinate \(q\) is
essential to the proved structural image.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed: The Ejaz--Bareinboim \(\rho\)-Markovian restriction in Definition 3.2 requires that no ground endogenous variable have an exogenous relational parent and permits a non-relational exogenous parent to be shared only by attributes of the same instance.  Separately, Section 5 assumptions (I)--(III) specify the neural-completeness domain, including finite observed domains and one uniform finite bound on relational-parent multiset size over every admissible skeleton in the declared domain.  Theorem 5.2 establishes RNCM expressivity, while Algorithm 1 together with Appendix D, Corollary D.7 in arXiv v2 supplies sound and complete neural identification on that Section 5 domain.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The current claim conflates the Definition 3.2 Markovian restrictions with the separate Section 5 neural-completeness assumptions and cites Corollary D.6 instead of the arXiv v2 correctness result, Corollary D.7.

\]

On an instance in the intersection of that domain with the Definition 3.2 \(\rho\)-Markovian class, suppose additionally that, for the same source laws and causal query, every model in \(Mone\) belongs to the corresponding Ejaz--Bareinboim compatible class. proposed_statement_changes.reason: The unconditional structural equality is unchanged, but upward comparator transfer requires an explicit same-data, same-query class inclusion on an instance in the Section 5 domain; sharp ranges and singleton identification do not transfer to a strict superclass.

proposed_assumptions.condition: In every source grounding in \(Rsrc\) and target grounding \(\rho\) admitted by \(G\), no ground endogenous variable has an exogenous relational parent.
proposed_assumptions.reason: This is one of the fully Markovian structural restrictions intended for the two compatible-SCM classes and is stated separately from exogenous independence.

proposed_assumptions.condition: In every source grounding in \(Rsrc\) and target grounding \(\rho\) admitted by \(G\), no non-relational exogenous variable is a parent of two distinct ground endogenous variables.
proposed_assumptions.reason: This makes explicit that the present structural classes exclude the within-instance sharing of a non-relational exogenous parent permitted by the comparator anchor.

proposed_assumptions.condition: Across all admissible skeletons admitted by \(G\) in the declared Ejaz--Bareinboim comparator domain of interest, the cardinalities of the relational-parent multisets of ground endogenous variables are bounded by one common finite integer.
proposed_assumptions.reason: This records the global Section 5 comparator-domain condition without inferring it from the finitely many listed source and target groundings and without adding it to either structural sharpness class.

proposed.condition: In every source grounding in \(Rsrc\) and target grounding \(\rho\) admitted by \(G\), the joint law of all distinct exogenous variables factorizes as the product of their marginal laws.

standard.name: Mutual independence of distinct exogenous variables

proposed_core_edits.reason: Independence of distinct exogenous variables is logically separate from prohibitions on exogenous relational parents and on a shared non-relational exogenous parent.

proposed.name: One-unseen-row compatible RSCM class
proposed.construction: \(Mone=\{M: M\text{ is a finite RSCM over }S\text{ and }G;\ M\text{ induces the source groundings }Rsrc\text{ and target grounding }\rho\text{ encoded by }Ictx,\text{ its distinct exogenous variables are mutually independent, no ground endogenous variable has an exogenous relational parent, no non-relational exogenous variable is shared as a parent by distinct ground endogenous variables, its finite mechanisms are type shared, it reproduces }Psrc,\text{ it uses the rows }K\text{ recovered from positive-probability source parent contexts, and it has exactly one unrestricted target-relevant binary row at }rstar\}\).

proposed_core_edits.reason: The replacement makes the already intended fully Markovian exogenous-parent restrictions explicit while excluding the comparator-only global parent-multiset bound.

proposed.name: Finite-unsupported-row compatible RSCM class
proposed.construction: \(\mathcal M_{\mathrm{fin}}\) is the class of finite RSCMs over \(S\) and \(G\) that induce the source groundings \(Rsrc\) and target grounding \(\rho\) encoded by \(Ictx\), whose distinct exogenous variables are mutually independent, in which no ground endogenous variable has an exogenous relational parent and no non-relational exogenous variable is shared as a parent by distinct ground endogenous variables, whose finite mechanisms are type shared, that reproduce \(Psrc\), use the recovered rows \(K\) at every target-relevant positive-source-support key, and leave precisely the target-relevant keys in \(\mathcal R_{\mathrm{free}}\) unrestricted over their native finite outcome alphabets.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The generalized structural class receives the same explicit fully Markovian restrictions as the one-row class, with no comparator-only global bound.

proposed.matched_by: The structural interval is sharp without the comparator-only global bound. On an instance in the Section 5 domain, nonconstant values transfer nonidentification only under an explicit same-data, same-query inclusion of the fully Markovian class in the Definition 3.2 compatible class; sharp ranges and singleton identification do not transfer to a strict superclass.

proposed.comparator_claim: Canonical finite SCMs reduce arbitrary discrete counterfactual sharp bounds to a polynomial program.
Polynomial programming yields numerical sharp or epsilon-sharp bounds and confidence-region relaxations for discrete causal queries.
Untrusted algebraic root certificates can be checked skeptically by verified univariate CAD and Sturm--Tarski computations.
Root counting and interval subdivision decide univariate polynomial relation systems soundly and completely in PVS.
Exact real-root isolation with multiplicities and nonsquare-free inputs has explicit polynomial bit-complexity bounds.
Unnested univariate parametric Markov-chain model checking is polynomial-time after the parametric model is explicit.
A response-signature LP gives tight causal-order bounds and constructs attaining SCMs.

proposed_core_edits.reason: The comparator promise now separates the Definition 3.2 class from the Section 5 domain and states exactly which implication is conditional.

prose_updates.tldr: For any finite family of target-relevant unsupported finite-categorical shared rows, the fully Markovian relational causal set is exactly the compact interval obtained as the image of an explicit rational polynomial over the product of row simplices, and both endpoints have common finite-noise type-shared RSCM witnesses. The one unsupported binary row remains the tractable specialization: derivative-root isolation gives exact algebraic endpoints and a skeptical certificate checks the complete relational instance and endpoint models with polynomial size and checking cost. The structural classes explicitly require mutually independent distinct exogenous variables, no exogenous relational parents, and no non-relational exogenous parent shared by distinct ground endogenous variables; they do not assume the comparator-only global parent-multiset bound. Ejaz--Bareinboim Definition 3.2 permits non-relational exogenous sharing only among attributes of the same instance, while their Section 5 neural-completeness domain is separate. On an instance in that domain, nonidentification transfers only under an explicit same-data, same-query class inclusion; neither the sharp interval nor singleton identification transfers to a strict superclass. Supported-row boxes use the multiplicative radius \(\delta_{\times}=1-\prod_r(1-\epsilon_r)^{m_r}\). The exhaustive assignment-level incidence grammar still has the stated treewidth-zero exponential obstruction.

project_justification.gap: The Ejaz--Bareinboim sound-and-complete neural identification result applies on its Section 5 domain but does not return the exact compatible causal range after nonidentification. Generic polynomial bounds likewise do not prove that every product-simplex parameter vector is realized by a type-shared fully Markovian RSCM or certify the relational derivation and endpoint models.
project_justification.niche: Finitely many unsupported finite-categorical rows admit an exact structural reduction to a rational polynomial on a product of simplices in an explicitly fully Markovian class. The one-binary-row case additionally admits efficient exact univariate algebraic certification. Comparator conclusions are stated only on the intersection with the published Section 5 domain and under an explicit compatible-class inclusion.
project_justification.fill: The project proves the multivariate structural sharp image with finite-noise endpoint witnesses, retains a sound and complete polynomial-size skeptical certificate for the univariate specialization, supplies a conservative sampling enclosure using a history-adaptive multiplicative occurrence-coupling radius, and separates its structural assumptions from the comparator-only global parent-multiset condition.

prose_updates.related_work: Ejaz and Bareinboim's Definition 3.2 separately requires no exogenous relational parent and permits a non-relational exogenous parent to be shared only by attributes of the same instance. Their Section 5 assumptions (I)--(III), rather than Definition 3.2 alone, specify the neural-completeness domain, including finite observed domains and one uniform finite bound on relational-parent multiset size over all admissible skeletons in the declared domain. Their Theorem 5.2 proves RNCM expressivity, while Algorithm 1 together with Appendix D, Corollary D.7 in arXiv v2 supplies sound and complete neural identification on that domain. The present exact image instead concerns the fully Markovian structural class with mutually independent distinct exogenous variables, no exogenous relational parents, and no non-relational exogenous parent shared by distinct ground endogenous variables; the comparator-only global bound is not a premise of structural sharpness. On a Section 5 instance, a nonconstant image proves comparator-class nonidentification only after a same-data, same-query inclusion is established. Neither the subclass interval nor a constant subclass polynomial transfers as a sharp range or point-identification result to a strict superclass. Zhang, Tian, and Bareinboim provide canonical finite-SCM polynomial programs, and Duarte et al. provide general numerical polynomial bounds and confidence-constraint relaxations; neither supplies this relational product-simplex realization theorem, exact univariate relational certificate, or multiplicative labeled-occurrence enclosure. Li, Passmore, and Paulson, Narkawicz, Mu\~noz, and Dutle, and Tsigaridas and Emiris supply the skeptical algebraic and root-isolation substrate. Hutschenreiter, Baier, and Klein identify a polynomial explicit-univariate model-checking core. Rossetto and Antonucci construct attaining models for order-based nonrelational bounds, but their witnesses do not impose the present type-shared fully Markovian semantics.
prose_updates.honest_scope: Structural soundness, completeness, compact interval form, endpoint attainment, and the finite breakpoint atom-count bound are proved for any finite family of unsupported finite-categorical rows in fully observed, acyclic, type-shared RSCMs with mutually independent distinct exogenous variables, no exogenous relational parents, and no non-relational exogenous parent shared by distinct ground endogenous variables. The structural result does not require the comparator-only uniform parent-multiset bound. Exact derivative-root optimization, algebraic endpoint comparison, polynomial-size certificates, the sharp optimizer-degree guarantee, and the at-most-two algebraic-noise-mass guarantee remain specific to one unsupported binary row. Comparator statements are restricted to instances in the Ejaz--Bareinboim Section 5 domain and require an explicit same-data, same-query inclusion in the Definition 3.2 compatible class. Even then, only nonidentification transfers automatically; the interval is not claimed sharp for a strict superclass, and singleton identification transfers only under class equality. Efficient exact multivariate optimization, compact circuit-level incidence, conditional postintervention queries, exact nuisance-box projection, and empirical usefulness beyond the documented N3 example remain open. The sampling enclosure has simultaneous coverage and uses \(\delta_{\times}\leq\min\{1,\sum_rm_r\epsilon_r\}\); it is deliberately conservative.
